subject.title: Support isolated native subagent workspaces with workspace-only skills

question: Should OpenClaw expose a native-only `sessions_spawn.workspace` capability for per-child workspace and skill-root isolation, or retain the current inherited-workspace model?
rationale: This is a new public agent-tool capability with a security boundary and persisted session semantics; code review cannot choose the durable product contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow native isolation contract
options.body: Approve a native-only, descendant-validated workspace parameter with workspace-only skill lineage and explicit ACP exclusion, subject to security and real-runtime proof.

options.title: Keep inherited workspace semantics
options.body: Decline the new per-spawn boundary and retain the current `cwd` plus inherited-workspace model for native subagents.

options.title: Request a smaller API design
options.body: Require the proposal to narrow to an existing agent or skill-visibility contract before accepting a new spawn parameter.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow native isolation contract
recommendation.body: Approve a native-only, descendant-validated workspace parameter with workspace-only skill lineage and explicit ACP exclusion, subject to security and real-runtime proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their earlier contribution is directly associated with the spawn workspace-resolution path, though current ownership should be confirmed by a maintainer.
